data.description: The driver took a significantly longer route from Orchard Central to Changi Airport T3. I normally take the PIE which takes about 35 minutes and costs around $28. On this trip the driver went through Geylang and East Coast area, taking 37 minutes and the fare was $35. The driver did not inform me about any route change or traffic. The extra distance was 4.3 km and I was overcharged. I am requesting a refund of the excess fare.

data.calculation: (actual kilometres - recommended kilometres) * distance rate; currency rounded to integer cents

policyRules.text: Rerouting for traffic, road closures or congestion is allowed, but the rider must be informed.
Before or at deviation the driver must inform the rider through in-app chat or verbally supported by the trip call recording, with a brief reason.

Deviation no greater than 1 km is within tolerance with no excess-distance refund. Above 1 km: traffic-justified and informed/agreed rerouting has no refund; traffic-justified but unnotified rerouting permits a partial refund of excess distance fare; unjustified rerouting requires the full excess distance fare refund. Category escalation in §6.2 still applies before an automatic ruling.

Deviation distance is actual route distance minus recommended route distance. Historical traffic evidence at the trip time verifies traffic justification. Chat or call evidence confirming acknowledgment establishes rider agreement.
A safety incident or safety-related allegation requires human review regardless of dispute category or amount.
For safety incidents, agents may gather and summarize evidence but cannot determine fault or recommend a resolution.

Dispute value under S$10 permits automatic determination at any confidence level; S$10 through S$50 requires confidence of at least 80%; above S$50 always requires human review. Category restrictions in §6.2 also apply.

Route deviation requires confidence of at least 80% AND deviation no greater than 2 km; otherwise human review. No-show/cancellation is eligible for automatic determination at its fixed S$5 fee. Safety always requires review.

The app charged me a $5.00 cancellation fee for a 'no-show' which is completely unfair — I was there, the driver was not. I want the charge reversed immediately.

data.details: Rider R-7823 booked trip TRIP-2026-09945 from Tiong Bahru Plaza to VivoCity. Scheduled pickup 08:45.

policyRules.text: The driver must wait at the pickup location for a free wait time of five minutes from the scheduled pickup time. After five minutes the driver may cancel for rider no-show.
The rider is charged a S$5 (500 cents) no-show cancellation fee when the driver cancels after the free wait period; the fee compensates the driver.

Before cancelling for no-show the driver must attempt at least one in-app chat message AND at least one phone call through the in-app calling system. Failure to satisfy both contact obligations voids the cancellation fee. An unanswered call is still an attempt; contact after cancellation does not qualify.

If the driver has not arrived by scheduled pickup plus five minutes, the rider may cancel without charge. If the driver fails to arrive AND fails to attempt contact, the rider is eligible for a separate S$5 goodwill credit. That credit is a distinct action from refunding a fee.
A safety incident or safety-related allegation requires human review regardless of dispute category or amount.
For safety incidents, agents may gather and summarize evidence but cannot determine fault or recommend a resolution.

Dispute value under S$10 permits automatic determination at any confidence level; S$10 through S$50 requires confidence of at least 80%; above S$50 always requires human review. Category restrictions in §6.2 also apply.

Route deviation requires confidence of at least 80% AND deviation no greater than 2 km; otherwise human review. No-show/cancellation is eligible for automatic determination at its fixed S$5 fee. Safety always requires review.

data.description: Final fare of $16.50 was charged, but the upfront quote shown at booking was only $12.00. The rider was not informed of any fare change, surge pricing, or price adjustment before or during the trip. The rider requests a refund of the $4.50 difference.

data.message: Hi, I'm at the taxi stand outside Bugis Junction near the fountain.
OK, I see you. Pulling up now, white Elantra.
Thanks for the ride! Just noticed the fare is $16.50 — I thought it was $12?

data.calculation: actual fare cents - quote cents; reconcile unchanged surgeable subtotal and unchanged fixed components

policyRules.text: The upfront quote is binding at the surge multiplier in effect when quoted.
An increase in surge before trip start requires an in-app notification before or at pickup stating the new multiplier, revised estimated fare, and an option to cancel without penalty.

When surge increases and the rider was not notified, refund the full surge differential. When properly notified and the rider proceeds, the higher fare applies. Lower surge benefits the rider; unchanged surge leaves the quoted fare applicable.
Surge differential = actual fare minus upfront quote, provided the difference is attributable solely to the multiplier change with all other fare components unchanged.
Booking fee is exempt from surge. Base fare, distance fare and time fare are multiplied.
A safety incident or safety-related allegation requires human review regardless of dispute category or amount.
For safety incidents, agents may gather and summarize evidence but cannot determine fault or recommend a resolution.

Dispute value under S$10 permits automatic determination at any confidence level; S$10 through S$50 requires confidence of at least 80%; above S$50 always requires human review. Category restrictions in §6.2 also apply.

Route deviation requires confidence of at least 80% AND deviation no greater than 2 km; otherwise human review. No-show/cancellation is eligible for automatic determination at its fixed S$5 fee. Safety always requires review.

claims.text: The verified surge multiplier increased from 1.0 at quote time to 1.5 at trip start, resulting in a $4.50 fare increase.
The supplied evidence shows the rider was not notified of this surge increase via the in-app notification required by policy.
The fare difference of $4.50 is solely attributable to the surge multiplier change, with all other fare components unchanged.

concessions: The rider's account that they were not informed of a fare change is supported by the verified lack of notification in the app record.

rider_brief.position: The supplied record establishes a policy basis for a refund of the $4.50 surge differential.

claims.text: The rider reports that the final fare was $16.50 while the upfront quote shown at booking was $12.00, and they were not informed of any fare change before or during the trip.
Verified records confirm the upfront quote was $12.00 (surge multiplier 1.0) and the final fare was $16.50 (surge multiplier 1.5), resulting in a $4.50 difference.
A derived fact, based on supplied evidence, confirms the $4.50 fare difference is solely attributable to an increase in the surge multiplier from 1.0 to 1.5, with all other fare components unchanged.
An app event record shows the surge multiplier increased to 1.5 at 21:04:30, before the trip start, and that the rider was not notified of this change.

Policy RYDE-V2.1-3.2 requires notification of a surge increase before or at pickup, and policy RYDE-V2.1-3.3 states that when surge increases and the rider was not notified, the full surge differential is to be refunded.

concessions: The trip was completed as scheduled, with the actual duration matching the estimated duration.
The driver's GPS data indicates movement from the pickup point consistent with a completed trip.
